source.title: Towards Safe Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models via Corrective Intervention
source.authors: Yi-Chi Zhang; Yue Ding; Jing-Wen Yang; Tian-Yuan Luo; Dong-Bai Li; Ran-Jie Duan; Qiang Liu; Hang Su; Yin-Peng Dong; Jun Zhu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: It measures tokenwise KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful trajectories, relevant to the positional-concentration claim, but does not establish concentration in the first few response positions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports harmfulness changes after replacing compliance cues with safety triggers. That is a corrective intervention, not a test of compliant prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes. Its safety-alignment fine-tuning results do not test harmful or ordinary benign fine-tuning as specified in V1 or V2.
record.test_reason: The paper studies safety in the chain-of-thought of reasoning models and proposes IPO, which swaps compliance cues for safety triggers before preference training. It cites Qi et al. (2025) only for its GPT-4o judge prompt. It does not fine-tune on harmful or benign data to measure eroded safety (V1, V2). It does not test prefilling, suffix or decoding bypasses (V4), localize safety in weights (V5), or test why safety is shallow (V6). It frames no training as deepening safety beyond the first tokens (V7). Its one KL analysis (Fig. 7) compares the authors' own IPO model with SFT baselines on tokens tied to compliance cues. That diagnoses their own method and says nothing about whether divergence concentrates in the first response positions (V3). Its CSR turning-point findings are a related but different construct: safety shifts at mid-reasoning steps in large reasoning models.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that harmful content persists in the chain of thought of existing safety-aligned reasoning models even when final answers are safe. Safe reasoning hinges on a few safety-trigger steps, and compliance cues predict unsafe continuations. IPO, preference learning on trajectories corrected at the first compliance cue, cuts harmfulness by over 30% relative to the best baselines while preserving reasoning ability.
record.recipe_differences: IPO replaces compliance cues with sampled safety triggers and trains on preference pairs; it is not harmful-example fine-tuning, benign-data fine-tuning, compliant prefilling, or a test of the cited first-token bypass methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The KL analysis compares IPO with SFT-based methods; the paper reports higher cue-correlated KL for IPO. The safety-trigger intervention is tested with three representative triggers, but the text gives no trigger-specific numerical results.

fits_no_version.finding: In DS-8B, over 90% of safe reasoning trajectories reach a stable high continuation safety ratio (CSR) at identifiable 'safety trigger' sentences. In unsafe trajectories, CSR turning points align with the first compliance cue (Pearson 0.85). Qwen3-8B shows the same pattern qualitatively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning models, whether the chain of thought stays safe is decided at a few mid-reasoning steps (safety triggers or compliance cues), not uniformly or only at the response opening.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing the first compliance cue with a sampled safety trigger sharply reduces how harmful the continuation is, and repeating the replacement reduces it further (figure-only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inserting a safety trigger mid-reasoning steers unsafe reasoning toward safe continuations.

record.problems: The relevant KL result is plotted and only qualitatively described; no positional KL values or uncertainty are stated. The CSR analysis uses 30 prompts and 32 sampled generations per token, and cue detection uses GPT-4o. Safety judgments elsewhere in the paper are also GPT-4o-based, with manual-consistency checks reported.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning of safety-trained models.
No benign fine-tuning measured for increased harmful compliance.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models over the first response tokens; Fig. 7 is organized around compliance-cue tokens and compares training methods.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding-based bypass of refusal; jailbreak benchmarks evaluate the authors' trained models only.
No test of data or objective causing shallowness.
IPO intervenes at mid-reasoning steps but is not framed or tested as spreading safety beyond the first tokens, and there is no prefill or fine-tuning-attack durability test.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and its V3 limits_scope label are not supported. The only KL result evaluates the authors' own method against baselines and is indexed by cue-correlated tokens, not by early response positions. Qi et al. (2025) is cited only as a source for the evaluator prompt. Safety judgments use GPT-4o, with manual agreement of 93.7% for reasoning and 88.3% for responses.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune safety-trained models on harmful examples to measure whether they begin complying.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning for increased harmful compliance.

The KL result is described as higher at tokens correlated with compliance cues, but the paper does not state that most divergence lies in the first few response positions or quantify its positional share.
Does not test compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Does not localize safety to a small set of weights or ranks.
Studies safety triggers and compliance cues, but does not test whether the data or training objective produces the claimed shallowness.
Does not test training intended to spread safety beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: DS-8B (IPO-aligned; base LRM used as reference)
rows.operation_detail: Visualizes per-token KL divergence between aligned LRM and base LRM, averaged over harmful trajectories.
rows.measure: Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base LRM.
rows.baseline: Base LRM is the KL reference; numerical baseline not stated.
rows.value: The text reports higher KL divergence on tokens correlated to compliance cues than for SFT-based methods; plotted values are figure-only.
rows.note: The text identifies cue-correlated tokens, but does not state that the divergence is mostly in the first few response positions or give numerical positional values.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own method (IPO) with SFT baselines, shown only in a figure. It reports KL at compliance-cue-correlated tokens, not by response position, so it cannot show V3's first-token concentration. It should not be linked to V3.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (DS-8B)
rows.operation_detail: Estimates continuation safety ratios along safe reasoning trajectories using sampled continuations.

conditions.value: 30 JailbreakBench prompts selected for uncertainty in completion safety

rows.measure: Share of sampled safe trajectories with a stable CSR turning point.
rows.value: Over 90% of sampled safe trajectories contain such turning points.
rows.note: This is a CSR trajectory measure, not per-token KL or a test of the first few response positions.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. This is a CSR trajectory statistic on 30 selected prompts, not a claim-version measure.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (DS-8B)
rows.operation_detail: Compares indices of unsafe-trajectory CSR turning points with indices of first compliance cues.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between compliance-cue indices and CSR turning-point indices.
rows.note: Reports association between cue and turning-point locations, not KL divergence or a causal test of the claim versions.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. It is a correlation between turning points and cue positions (r=0.85).

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (DS-8B)
rows.operation_detail: Replaces the first compliance cue in an unsafe trajectory with a sampled safety trigger, then evaluates continuation harmfulness; intervention may be repeated for remaining unsafe traces.
rows.measure: Harmful ratio of reasoning continuations after replacement.
rows.baseline: Continuation before replacement; numerical value not stated.
rows.value: The text reports a rapid decline in continuation harmfulness and a cumulative effect; numerical values are figure-only.
rows.note: This is corrective replacement with a safety trigger, not a test of compliant prefilling or another bypass method.
rows.check: The operation is mislabeled 'weight_edit'. It is an inference-time edit of the reasoning text: the first compliance cue is replaced with a safety trigger and generation continues. No weights are changed. Its values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Replicates the Continuation Safety Ratio analysis across reasoning trajectories.

conditions.value: Qwen3-8B, described as safer than the DeepSeek models

rows.measure: CSR changes around compliance cues and safety triggers.
rows.value: The text reports that CSR often drops sharply at compliance cues and can rise back toward 1 after safety triggers; event positions strongly correlate with eventual trajectory harmfulness.
rows.note: Qualitative replication; no numeric correlation or KL positional distribution is stated.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. It is a qualitative replication on Qwen3-8B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
